utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'm only getting sound. It was turned down very low. Yesterday you were asked about whether those people who were interrogated, why they weren't tried. Did you know how they were released or how it is that they weren't tried?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, from my testimonies so far and my statements, that I had -- that I was not in a position of authority with regard to any of these facilities. However, according to what I heard from my colleagues, they had interrogated all the people in Omarska. And based on that information, that is, the private conversations that I had, I learned that during the interrogations it was established that there had been preparations for possible war, and that referred, first of all, to making stocks of food and medicines that were found in bunkers at Kozarac. I didn't see that with my own eyes. That's not first-hand information. Based on those conversations my comment was: But how come that no criminal complaint was ever filed against them? That was my private comment. I wasn't present, as I said. I don't know what happened. But the last time I was here to testify about the same topic, the Zupljanin Defence said that criminal complaints were filed. I don't know, as I said. I played no part in that. I repeat, I was wondering how come that it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show 65 ter 20213 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you read this text, it says that this was -- this is a pardon of the 2nd of October, 1992, signed by Vojo Kupresanin on my behalf. Can you see the signature?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. It says Serbian Assembly of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know of any other cases of us having released even hardened criminals, because we wanted to exchange them for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not informed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- probably there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The question suggests that it has been established these people were criminals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue. The Chamber is cognisant of this. You are not giving evidence, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit D4211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us briefly show D2056.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at these names. Do you know them? Are these prominent people, these people that I pardoned in 1994? Can you please read what this decision is about.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decision on pardoning sentenced persons. Article (a), the sentenced Jusuf, son of Omer, Ramusevic, shall be released from serving a prison sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't need to read it all.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that there are people from our area, Seferovic, Causevic, and others. They must be from the Prijedor municipality, but I don't remember anyone individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you know that they had all been indicted and one of them was convicted?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not a question. It was just a reply to the objection of the OTP that it has not been established that they were convicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are not giving evidence. You did not follow the objection of Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hardly wait to give evidence, believe me. But since this is an exhibit already, I don't want to tender it. I just want to show that these people were tried.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first thing I hear, that some people were convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I don't follow this conversation. You are -- let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, but it is a perfect example of the problem with leading because if the witness hadn't noted that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just let's continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. But it emphasises the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miskovic, we're familiar with my position with regard to abiding by the law, and what was your attitude in that respect?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My attitude was generally known in Prijedor, but your position too, as I have already said in all my statements, that at the meetings where I was present your position was the same: Respect for the law, the constitution, and other rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The similar example is the -- our phone conversation after the referendum which was intercepted and was shown here in this court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us show 65 ter 32661.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 15th of November. When did our referendum take place, the plebiscite?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think it was after the one about the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina conducted by the Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need the fourth page in English and in Serbian it may be the third. Could we get the right page in Serbian. Let's see. No, it's not this one. I'm going to read from the English. It seems that we can't find it -- or maybe this is it. I guess this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please focus your attention where I say: "Good, excellent, you thought well ..." Do read it and especially the part under that. You don't have to read it out aloud. Just tell me what this is about. Thank you. Take a look at this. Let us see precisely -- this is to see exactly how to do it in a legal way, this part I mean. And it also says to see how to do it legally and then proceed with it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The relevant section seems to be on another page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How does this tally with your experience about our insisting on law and order?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this intercept you pointed out to me that I should contact Simovic and see to it that everything is done in a legal manner, but I never met him so that it remained an open issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember what this "it" was you were talking about, do it legally, in a legal way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the referendum, the referendum about remaining in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you confirm that you had a telephone conversation like this with Mr. Karadzic at the time? So this was you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is me. We already dealt with this at the trial of Stojan Zupljanin, the very same document, and it was identified that it was me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit D4212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday item 6 from your minutes was the topic of a question, a clear policy toward the non-Serb population should be defined. What was my position and the position of the party, bodies of the SDS, with regard to non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could get a reference. I don't recall any questions about an item 6 about a policy toward non-Serb population yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we get -- I believe it was admitted but I have a 65 ter number, 25720 is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P6592, proposal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I believe so, Mr. Miskovic's proposal, proposed measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I did ask about the proposal, but I did not ask about point 6, about the policy toward non-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's contained in the proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us hear the question. I interrupted you, Mr. Robinson, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was just going to say that would be really unfair to omit a point of a document and then preclude the other party from asking about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is the accompanying text, an excerpt from the minutes. And what I need is on page 3 in English and in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your experience, what was our policy towards non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general policy of the SDS and consequently the policy of the SDS in Prijedor was in favour of peaceful solutions in every field, and to that purpose it was our policy to conduct talks and negotiations in keeping with election results, and that's what we did all the time. You saw from my evidence yesterday and before that maximum efforts were made to avoid confrontation and conflict. The best confirmation that we were right is that Montenegro, which remained within the Federation at the time, later seceded, separated, itself from Yugoslavia peacefully and democratically.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D29 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, if you are moving away from this document. Solution, peaceful solution is one thing. Policy towards non-Serbian population may be another. What did you have in mind when you wrote this item number 6? Could you read it out? I'll read it: "To establish a general and unified policy towards the non-Serbian population." So what did you have in mind when you wrote "a general and unified policy"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain. I said yesterday that Prijedor was an exception because there was not a single excess on our territory against the Croat or the Muslim population, because we had this agreement and -- however, there were incidents in other municipalities of businesses being destroyed, et cetera. This had not happened in our municipality and that's why we wanted a general policy established to maintain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Please speak slowly. Yes, ask your question again, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 1st October, 1992. Can you tell us about all the things that happened before this date when this platform was endorsed?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense? Could you be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any war time conflicts?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday about the murder of that policeman, then the killing of those soldiers who were coming back from the war in Slavonia. They were ambushed at Hambarine. Then there was another roadblock of the Prijedor-Banja Luka road, although we had had an agreement about leaving all the communications open. And after that, there indeed was confrontation and conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D2910.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ensure full protection for non-Serb population. This is Karadzic's order to municipal authorities in mid-1994. This is about municipal authorities. And I was not part of that in 1994, I was not even head of the party because I had withdrawn in August 1993, so I don't know about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether this position that I took is consistent with our general policy of protection for minorities?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is consistent with the general attitude to non-Serb population that I discussed before. I can repeat if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit D4213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about discipline in the implementation of party decisions. Can you tell us which ideologies threatened at that time to be sneaked in as SDS policies? Which policies were risky?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday, but I'll repeat. Those were reformists and socialist forces, a legacy of the period before the multi-party elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In what forms were they active and through which institutions?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were represented in the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor and in the parliament legally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the ideology of JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were special. They were very attached to the ideology of the previous regime, and they found it very hard to abandon it. They were really indoctrinated by the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about the meeting of 23rd April, 1992, and generally our attitude to the JNA. You said the people where are concerned because young Serb men were in the JNA, whereas the Croats and Muslims were not. Tell us, what exactly was your concern regarding the fact that young Serb men were not in their homes, whereas the Muslims and Croats were?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, a general mobilisation was declared by the competent institutions, so that I, too, was mobilised in 1992 as the reserve police commander of the police station in Urije. The army conscripts were also mobilised, according to their military specialty, and sent to the theatre of war in Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you speak slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were being sent to the war zone in Slavonia, in Croatia. All the Serbs responded to the call-up; however, due to the Muslim propaganda and the propaganda of the Croat HDZ, who were appealing to their young men not to respond, very few Muslims and Croats responded to the mobilisation. And our area was empty of Serb military conscripts, whereas all the Muslim and Croat young men stayed at home. So the people were concerned and exerted great pressure on us, the politicians and the army, to do something about it. It's all a consequence of the experiences and memories from World War II, when all the able-bodied men who had stayed at home ended up in camps in Croatia, in Jasenovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you said there was pressure on you, politicians, and the army. Why you are taking their young men and leaving them without protection. That was not recorded. Is that what you said? What was the pressure about?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago because all the -- the people were exerting pressure because all the young Serbs over 18 were taken by the JNA and sent to the war in Slavonia. So as far as the Serbs were concerned, the homes were empty. However, because the Muslims and Croats did not respond to the call-up, their young men stayed at home, which left the Serb population without protection and vulnerable to organised attacks by Muslims and Croats, conditionally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Miskovic. I have no further questions. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Miskovic. On behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm happy if I made the smallest contribution to establishing the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is seized of the motion of Ratko Mladic for certification to appeal decisions of 11th of December, 2013, by Karadzic Chamber, which was filed yesterday. So I wonder whether the parties are ready to respond to this orally today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we filed a written response this morning and the response is that we don't object to the certification application but that Dr. Karadzic wishes to be the last witness at his trial. So we wanted you to take that into consideration in deciding the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not ready to respond in full orally at this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But then --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- but we will support the certification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes? Could you file a written response by close of business tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, we will do that, Mr. President. And as long as I'm on my feet, I don't want to pre-empt if the Court had other matters to discuss, but there's one other matter I wanted to raise before we adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. In keeping with our previous practice, Mr. Robinson and I met to discuss certain aspects of scheduling during the holiday period, and as we had done before we agree that a -- an extremely flexible regime should be adopted for what would otherwise be dead-lines for motions that need to be filed during this period of time. So we recognise that there may be certain motions for which there are specific and identifiable time sensitivities, the Court just raised one, for example. But barring that, it's our joint position that the dead-lines should be extremely flexible, in keeping with the limited staffing during this period. In particular, I might mention that the motion filed by the accused yesterday with respect to disclosure was one we would not be in a position to respond to without extraordinary measures until, for example, about January 13th. That's agreed. That general policy is the -- was what Mr. Robinson and I discussed and agreed to. I wanted to mention it to the Court and hope that the Court would endorse that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While the Chamber tends to agree in general -- do you like the Chamber to take specific actions in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I wouldn't -- I wouldn't think that was necessary, Mr. President. I tried to articulate it in a way that I thought would involve the least amount of specific intervention. So the idea would be barring some specific indication by one of the parties or by the Bench, that that particular matter falls outside this general approach, that whenever the responses to motions were filed would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think it's a polite way of asking us to keep quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Far be it for me to argue with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's endorsed, Mr. Tieger. I wonder whether there's any other matters to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, only on our behalf to thank the staff and the Chamber for all of its hard work this year to make this trial go smoothly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I would like to express my best wishes for the forthcoming holidays for all of participants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I wish everyone a very nice holiday and a happy new year. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of January, 2014, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.38 a.m.,
